editorial:
When a big-city TV host heads back to his small Southern hometown for his parents' anniversary, he expects a hero's welcome. Instead, he gets a reality check from the family he left behind. Martin Lawrence plays Roscoe Jenkins, a man who built a flashy talk-show career but never quite shook off his awkward childhood nickname. The movie leans hard into family chaos, sibling rivalry, and the kind of loud, messy love only relatives can deliver. It's a warm, silly comedy with a big ensemble cast that keeps the energy high from start to finish.

The cast is the real draw here. James Earl Jones brings gravitas as the tough dad, while Mo'Nique, Cedric the Entertainer, and Mike Epps steal scenes with sharp comic timing. The humor is broad and sometimes crude, so it won't be for everyone, but the heart underneath keeps it grounded. If you enjoy family reunion comedies with plenty of trash talk and a sweet payoff, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Roscoe stops trying to impress everyone and finally stands up for himself and his family. He confronts his rival cousin Clyde, makes peace with his father, and embraces his roots. The big twist is that Roscoe realizes his TV fame means nothing compared to the love of his family, and he chooses to stay connected to them. The movie ends with the family reunited and Roscoe finally earning his dad's respect.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and big ensemble casts.
